scope.reviewed: saved-flag gating and ordering, cursor increments, saved argument restoration, three callee interfaces, frame preservation

findings.result: Independent decode confirms a 68-byte body that saves row/item/group/auxiliary/flags in registers/stack and tests the original saved halfword flags: bit4 calls 4FC2 then advances the cursor by 4; bit7 reloads auxiliary and row/item/current cursor before calling 5054 then advances by 2; bit10 reloads row/item/cursor before calling 4F6E. Later gates use saved R5, not child-clobbered state. The 4FC2 call’s recovered interface is the three arguments R0-R2; the stored auxiliary R3 is not part of that contract and R3 may be scratch.

All 2,048 flag values 0..2047 pass isolated execution with each controlled child deliberately clobbering R0-R3. Ordered calls and cursor offsets match; R4/SP are preserved, and output replay JSON is byte-identical to the frozen candidate.
Source, exact body, and all receipt-listed artifacts match their pinned hashes. The corrected 002 packet avoids the earlier unsupported claim that 4FC2 receives a meaningful fourth argument.

limitations: All three callees are controlled; their behavior is not established.
Only flag values 0..2047 are enumerated; upper flag-bit behavior is not covered.
Physical field meaning, aliasing, concurrency, caller closure, and canonical admission remain unresolved.
